correctness.rationale: The forbidden tournament is complete, so a free amalgam cannot introduce it across the two sides, and the Fraïssé extension property realizes every valid finite extension over the named base. Homogeneity makes each ordered, distinct-new-vertex diagram a single orbit and hence a single complete type; distinct diagrams are distinguished by atomic formulas. A common adjacency on a triple with an arc can only close a cycle. This gives the stated unary and directed-pair conditions and t2=q^2+2R. For t3 the zero-arc term is q^3, the six oriented single-arc choices give 6qR, the two types of two-arc stars give the two square-sums with three choices of center, the oriented paths give six row-column products, and the two cycles give twice tr(A^3). An independent exact enumeration of all ternary base diagrams for n=0,...,5, with all relabellings and converses, recovered labelled counts (1,1,3,21,317,9735), class counts (1,1,2,5,17,79), and signature counts (1,1,2,5,17,78). It identified the sole collision (q,R)=(44,973) with the two stated representatives, and direct checks of all 21 new-triple diagrams gave 653452 and 658282. The underlying triangle versus K_{2,3} precludes converse-isomorphism. The frozen replay references are verify.cpp, crosscheck.py and verification_output.txt; the independent reproduction did not execute the uploaded code. This establishes only the claimed fixed-size reconstruction boundary and the specified separation.

value.rationale: Counting low-arity extension orbits is a concrete coarse reconstruction problem for the generic oriented structure. Reversal is an unavoidable ambiguity, so the first collision beyond it measures a genuine limit of these invariants. The result identifies that limit exhaustively, provides genuinely different underlying graphs at the collision, and shows exactly how the next arity resolves the ambiguity at the first failing order. That gives a usable small benchmark without asserting reconstruction above five vertices.
